data.title: SM Investments' nine-month net income rises 9% to PHP70 billion
data.description:
PASAY CITY, Philippines, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SM Investments Corporation (SM), the parent company of the SM Group, reported consolidated net income of PHP70.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 9% from PHP64.4 billion a year earlier.

Consolidated revenues increased 5% to PHP506.8 billion from PHP482.3 billion. Banking contributed 48% of consolidated net income, followed by property at 26%, retail at 15% and portfolio investments at 11%.

"Ongoing resilient consumer demand supported retail and malls, while portfolio investments delivered stronger earnings," said Frederic C. DyBuncio, President and Chief Executive Officer of SM Investments.

Consumer resilience

SM Retail posted net income of PHP13.1 billion, up 7% from the previous year, as consolidated revenues grew 5.4% to PHP335.3 billion. Growth was broad-based, supported by resilient consumer spending.

Food retail posted steady sales growth across its supermarket and minimart formats, reflecting continued demand for everyday essentials.

Specialty retail recorded higher sales, supported by demand for power-source alternatives and spending on selected discretionary categories, particularly toys, stationery and pet products.

Revenues from the Group's mall business increased 10% to PHP63.7 billion due to an increase in leasable space, higher occupancy and strong demand for dining and experiential offerings.

BDO Unibank's loan portfolio grew 16%, with double-digit increases across all segments while China Banking Corporation reported a 19% jump in net loans.

Portfolio performance

Meanwhile, portfolio investments accounted for 11% of consolidated net income, led by a turnaround in Atlas Consolidated Mining and Development Corporation as higher copper prices supported earnings.

2GO Group, Inc. recorded revenue growth of 15%, supported by strong performance across its businesses, particularly sea travel and container services.

Philippine Geothermal Production Company, Inc.'s 13% higher revenues were driven by higher steam prices which track the Wholesale Electricity Spot Market (WESM).

The parent advantage

The SM Group's businesses are largely in sectors that deliver strong predictable cashflows. Over 60% of parent annual cashflows are from non-listed businesses, including SM Retail, in addition to the dividends regularly received from listed subsidiaries.

All established businesses fund their own operations and expansion plans and do not require funding from the parent. With a strong balance sheet and reliable cash generation, SM Investments seeks to increase its returns to shareholders via higher dividends and an active share buyback program.

Total assets stood at PHP1.8 trillion as of September 30, 2026, with net debt-to-equity of 31:69.

"At the parent, we continue to allocate capital carefully and maintain the financial capacity to invest for the long term," Mr. DyBuncio said.

About SM Investments Corporation

SM Investments Corporation (SM) is an owner-operator of market-leading businesses in retail, banking, and property, with investments in high-growth opportunities in the Philippine economy. Through its portfolio, SM generates resilient cash flows and reinvests with discipline to compound value over the long term.

Its retail operations are the largest and most diversified in the country. Its property arm, SM Prime Holdings, Inc., is the largest integrated property developer in the Philippines. Its banking interests include BDO Unibank, Inc., the country's largest bank, and China Banking Corporation, one of the country's largest private domestic banks.

For more information, please visit www.sminvestments.com

SOURCE SM Investments Corporation

data.title: Bitcoin, Ether Edge Higher After Risk-Off Mood Drives Losses — Market Talk
data.description:
0847 GMT - Bitcoin and ether trade higher in early European trade, but fail to recover losses after heavy selling in the last session. A global tech selloff bled across other risk assets, Deutsche Bank analysts write, pushing bitcoin down to around $61,500--more than 29% lower than its September peak. The cryptocurrency trades at its lowest level since early July. Investor expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening also weigh on nonyielding digital assets. Bitcoin adds 0.8% to trade at $61,961, while ether gains 0.85% to trade at $1,754.(josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)

0831 GMT - Yields on U.K. government bonds, or gilts, fall as investors move funds from risk assets such as stocks to safer assets like government bonds. Fears about a possible slowdown in the AI industry are driving risk-off sentiment. Meanwhile the latest U.K. public finances data show borrowing in October came in at 17 billion pounds ($22 billion), while the borrowing estimate for the financial year to September was revised down by 3.6 billion pounds, to 94.3 billion pounds. Ten-year gilt yields fall 1.7 basis points to last trade at 5.298%, Tradeweb data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0821 GMT - The Hungarian forint remains under pressure after reaching a seven-month low against the euro overnight on the prospect of the National Bank of Hungary cutting interest rates and risk aversion. The NBH held rates at 5.5% earlier this week but signaled room for monetary easing. The currency is also under pressure due to an unwinding of carry trades, which involve borrowing in a low-yielding currency to invest in a currency with higher yields, ING's Chris Turner says in a note. The euro rises 0.5% to 372.83 forints after reaching as high as 373.57 overnight. "Any euro-forint close above the 373.65 upside gap from April would warn of an extension to 380," Turner says. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0816 GMT - U.K. public finances remain stretched, which could challenge the government's ability to maintain its fiscal rules, Pantheon Macroeconomics' Rob Wood and Elliott Jordan-Doak say in a note. The latest data show public borrowing stood at 17 billion pounds ($22 billion) in October, a 5.2% increase from a year ago. The October budget failed to address the main challenges facing U.K. finances, meaning the fiscal position could deteriorate further, the economists say. "We continue to have doubts about the government's ability to follow through on its fiscal plans, suggesting upside risks to borrowing in the coming years." (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0747 GMT - Sterling briefly edges higher after U.K. retail sales showed a rebound in October. Retail sales rose 0.7% on month, data from the Office for National Statistics show. The reading went against a consensus forecast of flat growth and came after a downwardly revised 0.6% decline in September. The ONS separately reports that public sector net borrowing in October was 17 billion pounds, better than the 18 billion pounds expected. Sterling initially rises to an intraday high of $1.3123 from $1.3115 before the data's release. The euro last trades at 0.8376 pounds, little changed from levels before the data, after briefly falling to an intraday low of 0.8370. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0741 GMT - U.K. retail sales data for October came in better than the September data, indicating that economic activity remains resilient, Omnis Investments' Patrick O'Donnell says in a note. Monthly retail sales rose 0.7% in October, following a 0.6% fall in September. "Whilst there is some evidence of a drag on real spending from rising fuel and utility prices and higher borrowing costs, the economy continues to hold up overall." (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0739 GMT - High borrowing costs on U.K. government bonds could continue to weaken public finances, Quilter's Kit Rees says in a note. Public sector finance data released on Friday show public borrowing stood at 17 billion pounds [$22 billion] in October, up 5.2% from the same period a year ago. Higher debt interest costs largely contributed to the increase. "Borrowing costs remain elevated and with further hiking from the Bank of England to come, the government is going to find itself increasingly hemmed in by the cost of its debt," Rees says. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0719 GMT - The dollar edges lower after Anthropic's record-breaking initial public offering failed to halt selling in U.S. AI-related stocks overnight. However, the dollar's pullback is modest, remaining near the 19-month high reached Thursday, supported by expectations for further interest-rate rises by the Federal Reserve. "As the global business cycle begins to lose momentum, we see the U.S. economy on a relatively stronger footing, and the solid domestic demand will allow the Fed to extend its hiking cycle further than peers," says Danske Bank's Kirstine Kundby-Nielsen in a note. The DXY dollar index is down 0.2% at 103.738, having reached 103.974 Thursday, its highest level since April 2025. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0712 GMT - Malaysia's export performance is expected to remain supported by resilient electrical and electronics shipments, alongside sustained demand for commodity-related products, particularly LNG and petroleum products, RHB senior economist Chin Yee Sian says in a note. The global technology growth cycle, driven by artificial-intelligence adoption and data-center investment, should support semiconductor demand, she says. Other manufactured exports, including chemicals, machinery and metal products, could also benefit from regional production and infrastructure spending, she reckons. However, a slowdown in AI-related investment, tighter U.S. chip controls and prolonged geopolitical disruptions could weigh on shipments, she adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

0704 GMT - Singapore's consumer-price index likely rose 1.9% on year in October, slowing from September's 2.2% increase, according to the median estimate of six economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. Core CPI, which excludes private road transport and accommodation prices, likely rose 1.6% in October, easing from September's 2.0% rise, according to the poll. The softer CPI prints expected will reflect the impact of lower electricity tariffs in 4Q, as well as high base effects, UOB economist Jester Koh says in a note. The data are due Monday.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0653 GMT - Japan's Nikkei Stock Average closed 5.1% lower at 56436.65, its lowest level since April 9. Chip and metals stocks led declines as enthusiasm over the artificial-intelligence trade continues to ebb. SoftBank Group dropped 14%, Kioxia Holdings lost 12% and JX Advanced Metals shed 9.5%. As investors seek the safety of government bonds and the yen, the 10-year Japanese government bond yield fell 3.5 basis points to 2.785%. The dollar is at 159.11 yen, down from Y159.70 as of 5 p.m. Eastern time Thursday. Investors are focusing on any signs of easing in AI and semiconductor stock selloffs as well as any developments in the wars in Iran and Ukraine following the U.S., Russian and Chinese leaders' trilateral summit this week. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)

0600 GMT - U.S. Treasurys rally in the Asian session on likely flight-to-quality flows. "The selloff in technology stocks drove safe-haven demand for Treasuries," Kenanga Research economists say in a note. Given a Fed rate increase in December is fully priced, "the key test is whether [coming U.S.] data supports further hikes priced for January and April 2027," they say. "We think markets overprice U.S. inflation risk, leaving room for front-end yields to ease further if the data cools," the economists add. The two-year Treasury yield falls 3 basis points to 4.7269% and the 10-year Treasury yield drops 3 bps to 5.0089%, FactSet data show. Bond yields move inversely to prices. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

data.title: Lenovo's Current Valuation Prices in Neocloud Exposure — Market Talk
data.description: Lenovo's current valuation has already priced in its exposure to neocloud, Citi analysts say, referring to specialized AI cloud infrastructure providers. The current valuation assumes 50% of its infrastructure-business profit is generated by neocloud customers and receives no valuation. This suggests limited downside risk and attractive valuation at current levels, Citi notes. Meanwhile, management stated neocloud clients only account for less than 20% of its infrastructure segment revenue, they note. "Cash-flow discipline, prepayment requirements and third-party financing mitigate neocloud client risk." Citi lowers Lenovo's target price to HK$36.70 from HK$40.00, taking a prudent view on the infrastructure business's future profit contribution amid limited visibility for AI infrastructure demand. Shares last ended 0.6% higher at HK$16.35.(sherry.qin@wsj.com)

data.title: Equinor Fends Off Cyberattack Detected Earlier This Week
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Equinor said Friday that it had stopped a dayslong cyberattack that had targeted some of its systems.

The Norwegian energy company detected the attack on Tuesday but said it wasn't a virus attack, so there was no chance of it spreading, and that it also didn't appear to be specifically targeting Equinor.

Production has been running as normal throughout, and there are no signs that data has been stolen or altered, it said.

"There is also no indication that the attack has had any negative consequences for employees, partners or suppliers," the company said.

Equinor has been in talks with national security authorities, and the incident has been reported to police.

Write to Dominic Chopping at dominic.chopping@wsj.com

data.title: China, HK stocks sink as Wall Street selloff dents sentiment
data.description:
Mainland China and Hong Kong stocks ended sharply lower on Friday, with tech shares leading losses after a steep Wall Street selloff weighed on investor sentiment, while Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO did little to revive waning optimism surrounding the artificial intelligence sector.

** By the close, the benchmark Shanghai Composite index dropped 1.2%, while the blue-chip CSI300 index lost 0.8%. Both indexes recorded their lowest closing levels since July 2025.

** For the week, the SSEC fell 2.8% to notch the biggest weekly drop since July, and the CSI300 lost 1.5%. Investor sentiment was also weighed down by signs that Washington is tightening tech curbs on China, despite meetings between the leaders of the world's two largest economies this week.

** The smaller Shenzhen index fell 3.6%, the startup board ChiNext Composite index tumbled 3.5% and Shanghai's tech-focused STAR50 index dropped 3.1%​.

** The decline came after US stocks slumped on Thursday, as AI-related shares came under pressure following Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO's failure to sustain an early rally.

** "The optimism failed to lift the broader AI sector, as concerns over stretched valuations and elevated capex spending continued to weigh on sentiment," analysts at OCBC said in a note.

** In China, tech sectors that require huge computing power, such as big data , AI and cloud computing (.CSI930851) all fell sharply.

** Hong Kong-listed shares of Chinese AI model developers, which rely heavily on advanced computing power, also tumbled.

** Minimax slumped 10.8% to record lows, bringing this week's loss to more than 30%. Z.AI shares declined 7.2%, bringing the weekly loss to 18.2%.

** Semiconductor shares were among the biggest drags, with a sub-index tracking the sector plunging 3.9%.

** Sentiment toward chipmakers was also hurt by Taiwan's TSMC tightening restrictions on Chinese chip designers, suspending some previously permitted advanced manufacturing orders and generally limiting affected customers to older chipmaking technology, sources told Reuters.

** Hong Kong's benchmark Hang Seng index fell 1.9% to the lowest intraday level since April 2025, while the city's tech shares lost 3.8%.

data.title: Euro zone bond yields fall as AI stock selloff boosts safe havens
data.description:
Euro zone bond yields fell on Friday as global stocks slid on doubts about the AI trade, sending investors towards safe-haven government debt.

Anthropic shares jumped in the company's blockbuster IPO on Thursday but did not revive excitement around the broader AI trade, with US futures and European shares dropping and Asian equities (.MISX00000PUS) set for their worst week since 2020.

Safe-haven German bonds benefitted, sending 10-year yields down 4 basis points to 3.368% (DE10YT=RR).

Two-year yields, which are more sensitive to central bank rate expectations, fell 5 bps to 3.111% (DE2YT=RR). Bond yields move inversely to prices.

French and Italian bonds (FR10YT=RR), also picked up, with yields down around 3 bps.

Euro zone bond yields have fallen from multiyear or multidecade highs in September and October as energy prices have cooled and tech stocks have dropped.

Oil prices held steady on Friday, with Brent crude at around $92 a barrel, down sharply from $118 a barrel in late October.

data.title: Indian central bank clarifies forex reporting rules for service imports, exports
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India on Friday clarified the scope of foreign exchange reporting rules governing services imports and exports that went into effect in October and sparked questions about whether they apply to resident individuals.

Earlier this month, the central bank had exempted resident individuals from declaration requirements and introduced a threshold of 1 million rupees ($10,760.79) for certain reporting obligations.

The RBI on Friday issued a set of frequently asked questions governing services trade transactions. Here are some details:

  • The central bank clarified that the 1 million-rupee threshold applies to each inward remittance and not the aggregate amount of receipts

  • Non-individual service exporters receiving over 1 million rupees are required to file an export declaration form (EDF) before the credit of proceeds

  • Authorized banks can extend EDF filing deadlines if they consider exporters' reasons to be justified. Banks will be required to publish trade-related policies and key operating procedures on their websites

  • The RBI notified the original rules governing reporting requirements in January, and they went into effect on October 1

  • "These new regulations are designed to align with evolving global trade practices and aim to significantly enhance the ease of doing business," it said in a Friday statement

($1 = 92.9300 Indian rupees)

HONG KONG, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Vitasoy International Holdings Limited ("Vitasoy" or the "Company", together with its subsidiaries, the "Group", Stock Code: 00345) today announced its interim results ended 30 September 2026 ("the interim financial period").

In the interim financial period, the Group's revenue increased by 3% to HK$3,337 million, supported by favourable foreign exchange translation movements. The Group's gross profit margin rose steadily to 51.9%, mainly attributable to the impact of favourable foreign exchange movements, effective raw material cost management and improved operational efficiency. Profit attributable to equity shareholders of the Company increased by 8% to HK$185 million.

Mr. Winston Yau-lai Lo, Executive Chairman of Vitasoy International Holdings Limited, said at the press conference today, "We will continue to evolve our business model to improve performance, with a deliberate focus on strengthening the Chinese Mainland operation. We will expand our presence in the snack channel and improve our execution in the declining general trade segment. Intensifying price competition, elevated oil prices and a restructuring of the Australian business that refocuses on ambient products is expected to have a significant negative impact on our profitability in the second half of the financial year. Nevertheless, we remain committed to driving down costs and operating with a high level of efficiency to generate sustainable long-term returns for shareholders."

Based on the Group's financial performance and cash position, the Board of Directors has declared an interim dividend of HK4.0 cents per ordinary share (previous interim financial period: HK4.0 cents per ordinary share), payable on 18 December 2026.

Chinese Mainland –Slight decline in revenue in local currency terms with a double-digit operating profit margin; improving sales performance via evolving channel mix following strengthened commercial leadership capabilities.

In the Chinese Mainland, the snack channel achieved double-digit growth year-on-year, a strong indicator of a preference for the brands among consumers, although this was offset by the declining general trade. Meanwhile, despite the market decline of plant milk in grocery channels, VITASOY gained market share in both the soy milk and plant milk categories during the interim financial period.

To maintain leadership in this competitive market environment, the Group strengthened the internal leadership, execution and innovation capabilities to win customers and capture emerging growth opportunities. The portfolio was enriched with VITASOY Jasmine Tea Soyabean Milk and VITASOY Coffee Latte Flavoured Soyabean Milk, as well as VITA Da Hong Pao Finger Lime Lemon Tea to broaden consumption occasions.

Through proactive cost management and enhanced operational efficiency, Chinese Mainland expanded the operating profit margin to 13% during the interim financial period.

Hong Kong Operation (Hong Kong SAR[1], Macau SAR[2] and Exports) –Solid leadership in soy and plant milk beverages in Hong Kong SAR supported by strong brand heritage, though performance was slightly offset by weaker demand in the Macau SAR business.

The Hong Kong Operation maintained its market-leading position in the Hong Kong SAR and achieved stronger performance in export markets. However, overall business results were tempered by softer performance in the Macau SAR operations.

The long-standing brand heritage and pervasive presence in the Hong Kong SAR, together with effective product strategies and operational excellence, accounted for the stable performance achieved during the interim financial period. Leadership was maintained in the non-alcoholic beverage segment, with dominant market shares in the soy and plant milk categories and steady expansion in the ready-to-drink tea category.

Recent product innovations received a positive reception across key segments, including VITASOY Jasmine Tea Soyabean Milk, VITASOY Coffee Latte Flavoured Soyabean Milk and VITASOY CALCI-PLUS 15g Protein Soya Milk in plant-based milk, alongside VITA Da Hong Pao Finger Lime Lemon Tea, VITA Fresh Tea, and VITA No Sugar Tea in the tea portfolio. In particular, the revamped visual identity and packaging of No Sugar Tea offerings helped renew consumer interest and supported strong sales momentum.

Exports to the US market demonstrated encouraging growth after the stabilisation of tariffs, supported by a pipeline of proven product innovations and a localised marketing campaign. Meanwhile, the Vitaland business recovered mainly due to improved performance in tuckshops and a higher number of school days.

In Macau SAR, performance was constrained by softer demand and mounting price pressure from new entrants as well as established competitors. Following the implementation of a strengthening plan to adjust pricing and enhance product visibility, the business in this market has begun to show signs of recovery.

Australia and New Zealand –Intensified price competition in a mature plant milk market and higher oil prices led to lower Australian dollar sales and a higher operating loss.

In Australia, intense market competition in the mature plant-based milk category and cautious household spending moderated topline recovery. Concurrently, New Zealand's revenue growth was offset by foreign exchange depreciation.

During the interim financial period, gross profit margin improved, supported by a favourable net sales price variance and lower raw material costs. However, operating profit recovery was hindered by higher packaging and transportation costs from rising oil prices, coupled with foreign currency fluctuations. We prioritised marketing initiatives to support the brand campaign and a packaging refresh, successfully increasing brand awareness and strengthening consumers' perceptions of the products' health benefits among plant-based milk consumers.

Singapore –

Robust revenue growth driven by strong demand for the tofu and beverage offerings.

Robust demand for Vitasoy's tofu and beverage offerings was a key driver of business growth for the Singapore business. Domestic sales gained positive momentum, led by volume expansion across both categories. Total revenue was up by 9% in local currency terms, accompanied by enhanced operating profitability.

The Philippines (Non-Consolidated Joint Venture) –

The joint venture with Universal Robina Corporation in the Philippines will continue to advance towards its long-term growth potential. Supported by strong in-store visibility and execution amid the growth of the plant-based milk segment in the Philippines, Vitasoy remains confident in its ability to scale up the operation and strengthen market presence.

For more details, please refer to the following documents:

  • Announcement of interim results ended 30 September 2026:Link
  • Photos download:Link

  • Note:

  • [1] "Hong Kong SAR" stands for the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China.

  • [2] "Macau SAR" stands for the Macao Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China.

About Vitasoy

Vitasoy International Holdings Limited is a leading manufacturer and distributor of plant-based food and beverages. Established in 1940 by the late Dr. Kwee-seong Lo in Hong Kong China, the Company strives to promote sustainable plant-based nutrition through provision of a variety of high-quality products with Nutrition, Taste and Sustainability as the guidelines for its portfolio offerings. Currently, Vitasoy has operations in China, including the Chinese Mainland and Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Australia, Singapore and the Philippines. Its products are available in about 40 markets worldwide.

Vitasoy is listed on the main board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (00345.HK) and included as a constituent of Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) Hong Kong Small Cap Index, Hang Seng Composite Index and Hang Seng Corporate Sustainability Benchmark Index, among others.

Vitasoy website: www.vitasoy.com

data.title: Gold, Silver slide to 14-month lows as Dollar, Fed fears bite
data.description:
Gold and silver fell sharply on Friday, with both metals hitting their lowest levels since September 2025, as a stronger US dollar and expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes drove selling across precious metals markets.

MCX December gold was trading at ₹1,22,435 per 10 grams at 9.04 am, down ₹5,017 or 3.94 per cent, while MCX December silver fell ₹9,448 or 6 per cent to ₹1,48,034 per kg. On the international front, COMEX gold futures were quoted at $3,551.90 per ounce, down 3.6 per cent, while COMEX silver traded at $42.44, down 4.33 per cent.

The sell-off follows a week of heavy losses. According to Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst at LKP Securities, gold has seen a correction of “more than ₹6,000 over the last two sessions,” with COMEX gold “facing resistance below $3,750.” He added that “the US Federal Reserve’s December policy meeting will remain the key trigger, with dollar strength, inflation expectations and the Fed’s policy guidance likely to determine the next directional move.”

The Axis Direct commodities report for November 20 placed gold’s short-term price regime as bearish, with a trend score of -4, noting that “weak sentiment and a technical sell-off” drove prices lower. data.title: Nifty hits 10-month high at midday; Apollo Hospitals, Axis Bank lead rally
data.description:
Benchmark indices reversed their gap-down opening to trade firmly in the green by mid-session on Friday, November 20, 2026, with the Nifty 50 touching a fresh 10-month high. At 12.40 pm, the Sensex was at 83,780.72, up 758.97 points or 0.91 per cent from its previous close of 83,021.75, having opened at 82,558.25. The Nifty 50 was trading at 25,730.75, up 216.45 points or 0.85 per cent from its previous close of 25,514.30, after opening at 25,368.00, a sharp intraday reversal of nearly 363 points from the opening level.

The recovery was broad-based at the index level, though market breadth on the BSE told a more cautious story. Of 4,344 stocks traded, 1,619 advanced while 2,482 declined and 243 remained unchanged. A total of 94 stocks hit 52-week highs against 118 touching 52-week lows, while 203 stocks were locked in lower circuits compared to 124 in upper circuits. BSE’s total market capitalisation stood at ₹5,13,66,483 crore, or approximately $5.5 trillion.

Apollo Hospitals, Axis Bank lead Nifty gainers

Apollo Hospitals led the Nifty 50 gainers, surging 5.33 per cent to ₹9,204.00 against a previous close of ₹8,738.00, with volumes of 9.55 lakh shares worth ₹868.87 crore. Axis Bank climbed 4.21 per cent to ₹1,439.00 from ₹1,380.80, trading 99.36 lakh shares valued at ₹1,396.03 crore, making it the highest-value trade among the day’s top gainers. Max Healthcare gained 3.74 per cent to ₹1,079.55, while TCS rose 2.83 per cent to ₹2,409.00. Bajaj Finance added 2.82 per cent to ₹1,123.65, with 57.39 lakh shares changing hands worth ₹632.44 crore.

SBI Securities noted that HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and ICICI Bank were the top three contributors to the Nifty’s gains, with banking stocks providing the primary thrust to the rally. IT emerged as the best-performing sectoral index, staging a sharp rebound from its 200-day exponential moving average. Metals were the worst performers, falling more than 2 per cent, consistent with declines in global commodity markets. The rupee extended gains to around 93.10 against the US dollar, adding mild pressure to domestically-priced commodity futures.

Titan, Tata Steel among top Nifty losers

On the losing side, Titan declined 2.18 per cent to ₹4,597.40 from a previous close of ₹4,700.00. Tata Steel fell 1.68 per cent to ₹177.86, with heavy volumes of 344.27 lakh shares worth ₹605.65 crore, the highest volume among Nifty losers. JSW Steel dropped 1.44 per cent to ₹1,317.50, while Hindustan Unilever shed 1.24 per cent to ₹2,048.40. Shriram Finance declined 1.06 per cent to ₹963.00.

Gold and precious metals remained under significant pressure. COMEX gold was trading around $3,524, down approximately 4.4 per cent, breaking below $3,550 for the first time since September 2025. COMEX silver plunged roughly 6.8 per cent to around $41.35. On the domestic front, MCX gold was down approximately 3.7 per cent near ₹1,22,790 per 10 grams, while MCX silver fell around 5.2 per cent to ₹1,49,230 per kg. MCX crude oil was down 1.5 per cent near ₹7,755 per barrel, tracking WTI crude which was trading around $82.90.

data.title: HDFC Bank surges 1.6% as banking stocks rally to fresh highs
data.description:
HDFC Bank shares jumped 1.61 per cent to ₹835 on the NSE on Friday morning, their strongest single-session gain this week, as the broader banking sector rallied sharply with Bank Nifty crossing the 63,000 mark for the first time.

The stock opened at ₹815.50, hit an intraday high of ₹836.75 and was trading with significantly higher volume than recent sessions, 345.33 lakh shares worth ₹2,863.50 crore by midday, more than double Wednesday’s traded value.

Buy-side participation also improved, with buyers accounting for 33 per cent of total traded quantity compared to roughly 23 per cent on Thursday, though sellers still held a two-to-one edge.

The move appeared driven by sectoral tailwinds rather than stock-specific triggers, with Bank Nifty surging past its previous all-time high of 62,442 to trade near 63,022, a gain of over 9,000 points in just 16 sessions.

The week’s gains have trimmed HDFC Bank’s year-to-date loss to 15.61 per cent from over 18 per cent earlier in the week, though the stock remains nearly 20 per cent below its 52-week high of ₹1,017.50 from December 2025. On a one-week basis, the stock returned 4.04 per cent, outpacing the Nifty 50’s 2.01 per cent.

At ₹835, the stock trades at a P/E of 15.83, still near multi-year valuation lows.

data.title: Beijing to bar young 'red-chip' firms from listing outside mainland China, sources say
data.description:
China's securities watchdog has told some law firms it will not approve plans by red-chip firms to list outside mainland China, people familiar with the matter said, a move that tightens its control of capital raised offshore and is a blow to Hong Kong's IPO market.

Red-chip companies are registered abroad, mainly in tax havens, but hold assets and businesses in China via equity ownership or contractual agreements.

The structure is favoured by Chinese startups, particularly tech firms, keen to raise capital in places like Hong Kong or New York to take advantage of more relaxed rules and deeper pools of funds available from foreign investors.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has told law firm representatives in recent days that red-chip companies established after the introduction of new offshore listing rules in 2023 must be re-domiciled in China before they can list, said the people.

The people declined to be identified as the regulatory guidance was confidential. The move is being reported for the first time by Reuters.

China and the US are competing fiercely to gain the upper hand in tech, particularly in AI and semiconductors, which has led to efforts by Chinese authorities to sharpen their scrutiny of technology, data and capital going outside its borders.

The CSRC did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Oversight of red-chip firms has gradually become stricter.

Prior to March 2023, Chinese companies employing overseas holding structures to raise capital abroad did not need regulatory approval. That changed with the advent of the new rules.

Then this year, the CSRC told Reuters in March that it was examining the "necessity and compliance" of red-chip structures, particularly those formed after March 2023.

Despite that warning, some red-chip IPO hopefuls and their advisors have been seeking approval to list outside the mainland without dismantling their existing structure and shifting their domicile back to China, one of the people said.

Most of those applicants failed to convince the regulator that a red-chip structure was necessary, prompting the tougher stance, the person added.

data.title: Taiwan October export orders surge by fastest clip on record thanks to AI demand
data.description:
Taiwan export orders rose more than expected in October to $123.82 billion and at the fastest clip on record, buoyed by worldwide demand for the island's AI chips and technology.

Here are some details from the Economy Ministry statement on the data released on Friday.

  • Export orders jumped 78.3% from a year earlier, the fastest rate ever and the third straight time that they had topped the $100 billion mark for a single month

  • The 21st straight monthly gain, it beat analysts' expectations for a rise of 64.3%

  • The ministry cited strong demand for AI, high-performance computing and cloud services applications

  • For November, it said it expected export orders to rise by between 57.6% and 62.7% from a year earlier

  • Uncertainties including geopolitical risks and trade policies would continue weighing on global economic growth, it said, while predicting that the spread of AI would support orders

  • Orders from Taiwan, home of the world's largest contract chipmaker TSMC and other tech companies, are considered a bellwether of global technology demand

  • October orders for Taiwanese telecoms products were up 107.2% from a year earlier, while those for electronic products jumped 89.8%

  • Orders from China were up 43.1% after a 48.5% rise in September, from the US they rose 96.3%, compared with a 79.4% rise the previous month, from Europe, they were up 61.8% and from Japan they rose 43.8%

data.title: Yomiuri: NTT, Swedish Firm to Explore Space-Ground Optical Communications
data.description:
By Takahiro Tsujimoto / Yomiuri Shimbun Staff Writer

NTT Inc. has signed a memorandum of understanding with SSC Space AB, a Sweden-based company providing space-related services, to collaborate in the field of optical communications between space and the ground, the Japanese telecommunications company announced Friday.

By combining NTT's optical communications and network control technologies with SSC Space's expertise in ground station operations, the two companies aim to create an optical communication infrastructure that connects space and the ground.

Under the memorandum of understanding, signed Nov. 11, the two companies will exchange information regarding the optical satellite communications market, customer needs and technological trends. They will also examine interoperability of their respective technology and service environments, as well as service integration with terrestrial networks.

Space-related businesses have been attracting attention in recent years.

In the communications sector, expectations are growing for high-speed, high-capacity, stable optical communications, given the increase in data transmission between space and the ground.

NTT is also focusing on developing space-ground network control technologies, as well as technologies that enable satellites to process data in space.

SSC Space is a public corporation that provides space infrastructure services in an integrated manner, including satellite launches and ground station networks.

"With ground station infrastructure around the world, and a long track record of supporting global satellite communications, SSC Space is a highly valued partner in advancing this initiative," Minako Tsumenaga, a senior vice president of NTT, said in a statement.

----

data.title: Alibaba's Cloud Business Faces Near-Term Hurdles; Long-Term Growth Supported — Market Talk
data.description: Alibaba's cloud outlook is likely to be dragged by reduced access to overseas advanced chips in the near term, while growth in the long term is assured, analysts say. They note that management has cut its cloud unit's growth outlook to 30% to 45% on year in fiscal year 2028. However, Daiwa thinks Alibaba has the potential to reaccelerate cloud growth to over 50% levels in fiscal year 2029. This will be driven by more AI chip supply coming from its in-house chip unit and improvement in broader domestic chip design and manufacturing capacity. Deep commercial relationships with domestic foundries will also help, the analysts say. Daiwa keeps a buy rating, and cuts target price to HK$155.00 from HK$180.00. Shares last traded at HK$83.40. data.title: Japan sets February start for full-scale rare earth seabed mining test
data.description:
Japan will begin full-scale test mining of mud rich in rare earths from the deep seabed off Minamitori Island, about 1,900 km (1,200 miles) southeast of Tokyo, on February 2, the head of the government-backed project said on Friday.

  • The 50-day test will be followed by a comprehensive evaluation, including economic feasibility aspects, Shoichi Ishii, program director of the Cabinet Office's national platform for innovative ocean developments, said

  • Japan plans to compile the findings into a report by March 2028, Ishii said

  • "We are still in the phase of testing and research toward industrialization," Ishii said, adding that the test aims to identify obstacles to moving from research and development to commercial operations

  • Japan and the US will share the results of their research and development activities, he said

  • Securing a stable and diversified supply of rare earths and avoiding excessive dependence on any single country was a higher priority than the project's economic feasibility, he said

  • He cited a sharp rise in the price of yttrium, a heavy rare earth that has been subject to Chinese export controls since 2025: "The price of this rare earth has become 180 times what it used to be"

  • The project has received a cumulative budget of about 50 billion yen ($314 million) from April 2018 through March 2027

  • Analysis of rare-earth-rich mud retrieved from the seabed earlier this year found that medium and heavy rare earth elements accounted for about 54% of its total rare-earth content

  • In February, Japan said it had successfully retrieved rare-earth-rich mud for the first time from depths of around 6 km

  • The project is part of Tokyo's efforts to reduce its reliance on China for critical minerals as Beijing tightens controls on rare-earth supplies

($1 = 159.0900 yen)
